*Last updated: October 16, 2026*

Alexandria is a Greek and Latin reader for iPhone and iPad, developed by
J. Tyler Kirby. Reading, dictionary lookup, and grammatical analysis run on
your device. You do not need an Alexandria account to use the app.

## Your reading and study data

Alexandria saves data on your device so you can continue reading and studying.
This includes:

- Reading positions, completion status, reading history, and statistics.
- Vocabulary, definitions, notes, example sentences, and saved passages.
- Practice cards, review schedules, results, mastery, and achievements.
- Reading-list selections, bookmarked lists, and personal collections.
- Words you flag for review, including the word, analysis, issue category,
  source text, and surrounding sentence.

Display and reading preferences, such as theme and font size, are also stored
on your device. The app has no advertising or third-party analytics SDKs.

## Optional iCloud sync

When iCloud sync is enabled, Alexandria uses Apple's CloudKit to store the
reading and study records listed above in your private iCloud database and
sync them between your devices. This includes saved words, notes, and passage
text, not just positions and bookmarks. The app does not send a word-lookup
request to a developer-operated analysis server.

Sync uses your Apple Account and an internet connection. You can change the
sync preference in Alexandria's Settings; restart the app to apply that
change. Turning sync off stops the app from syncing after restart. It is not
a request to erase existing iCloud records.

Your private CloudKit records are not sent to the developer as support
reports. Apple operates iCloud under its [privacy policy](https://www.apple.com/privacy/).

## On-device diagnostics and Apple services

Alexandria uses Apple's MetricKit to receive crash, hang, CPU, and disk-write
diagnostics on iPhone and iPad. It keeps up to 20 recent diagnostic records in
an on-device file, including the app version, receipt date, error details, and
a shortened call-stack summary. Diagnostic summaries are also written to the
device's system log. Alexandria does not upload this diagnostic file to the
developer or sync it through its private CloudKit database.

Apple's own diagnostics and distribution services have separate privacy
practices. In particular, TestFlight automatically collects beta crash logs
and usage information and shares them with the developer; feedback you send
through TestFlight is shared as well. See Apple's
[TestFlight privacy notice](https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/data/en/test-flight/).
This is separate from Alexandria's on-device diagnostic file and from the
private reading and study records described above.

## Sharing, exports, and support

Flagging a word saves a record in the app; it does not automatically send a
message to the developer. You can choose to export flagged words or share a
saved passage. Developer recovery tools can also export a user-data backup
or a sync diagnostic report. Backups contain your stored reading and study
records. Sync reports contain app/build information, record counts, sync
status, timestamps, and error details.

If you export a file, the destination you choose determines where it is stored.
If you share it or send it with a support request, its contents are available
to the recipients and services you select. Review files before sharing them.
The developer receives your email address, message, and any attachments when
you choose to contact support.

## Deleting data

You can delete individual saved items in the app. Settings also offers resets
for reading progress, vocabulary, reading statistics, or all user records.
When sync is enabled and functioning, saved record deletions can propagate to
iCloud and your other devices. Allow sync to finish before disabling it.
Reset Everything clears the app's stored reading and study records; it does
not clear the on-device diagnostic file, exported files, copies held by other
recipients, or all device preferences. The diagnostic file replaces its oldest
records as new records arrive, up to the 20-record limit. Resetting Alexandria
also does not delete diagnostics or feedback already held by Apple or a recipient.

Deleting the app from a device does not erase its existing iCloud data.
Manage cloud data through Apple's iCloud storage controls. See Apple's
[third-party app data guidance](https://support.apple.com/en-gb/guide/icloud/mm62d92d6b3e/icloud)
and [app deletion guidance](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/guide/iphone/iph248b543ca/27/ios/27).
Device backups and exported copies have their own storage and deletion controls.

## Website beta signup

The beta signup form on the Alexandria website is separate from the app.
Submitting it sends your name, email address, and optional institution through
Web3Forms to the developer's inbox to arrange a TestFlight invitation. Web3Forms
processes that submission as a service provider. Apple operates TestFlight.
Contact the developer to request deletion of signup information held by the
developer. Do not include sensitive reading or study information in the signup
form.

## Children and content

The app does not ask for a birth date or require an Alexandria account. Its
library contains classical literature and scholarly dictionary entries.
Consult the App Store listing for the current age rating and content descriptors.
